chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Uqda said: Muhammad ibn Salim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi narrated to us in Shawwal in the year 261 AH, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Rabat narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abd al-Rahman al-Qasir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: (And those who disbelieve say, 'Why is not a sign sent down to him from his Lord?' Indeed, you are only a warner, and for every people is a guide.)
He said: The Messenger of Allah is the Warner, and Ali is the Guide. By Allah, it has not departed from us, nor has it ceased to be among us until the Hour.

key_terms.الْمُنْذِرُ: The Warner (referring to the Prophet Muhammad)

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'Guide' mentioned in the verse 'And for every people is a guide' according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (as) elucidates the Quranic verse 13:7 by assigning the title of 'Warner' (Mundhir) to the Prophet Muhammad (saww) and 'Guide' (Hadi) to Imam Ali (as), establishing a complementary duality in divine leadership. This interpretation underscores the Shia doctrine of the continuity of guidance (Tawatur al-Huda), affirming that the capacity to guide the faithful remains an intrinsic, unbroken attribute of the Ahl al-Bayt until the Day of Resurrection.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (40) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed bin Abdurrahman bin Oqda narrated from Muhammad bin Salim bin Abdurrahman al-Azdi from Ali bin al-Husayn bin Rabat from Mansoor bin Hazim from Abdurrahman al-Qasseer that Imam Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said
when talking about the verse (You are only a warner and (there is) a guide for every people):

“The Prophet (S) is the warner and Ali is the guide. By Allah, it (the mission) has never been away from us and it will still among us until the Day of Resurrection. May Allah make us do what pleases Him!”
